title: Wartime Housing, Airport Lease & Zoning Fights
summary:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council's January 4, 1945 meeting:

*   **Post-War Housing for Veterans:** The city committed to supporting a survey and applying for federal aid to create more adequate housing facilities near the University of Texas for returning WWII servicemen and graduate students.
*   **Wartime Airport Lease:** Austin Municipal Airport was authorized for lease to the United States government, to be used as an auxiliary landing field in support of national defense efforts.
*   **Residential Zoning Protected:** A public hearing resulted in the denial of a request to rezone property on East 7th Street from residential to commercial, with the council upholding the area's residential character despite commercial arguments.
*   **Local Infrastructure & Permits:** The council approved the installation of a new water line across Lamar Boulevard for the International-Great Northern Railroad and granted a significant number of taxicab driver permits, including many to military personnel stationed at Bergstrom Field.

Commissioners Perry, Jones, and Wirtz of the Austin Housing Authority presented to the
Council a letter received by said Authority from the Texas Veterans Advisory Service
relative to provision by the Federal Board of Public Housing for living units for married
ex-service men and graduate students at the University of Texas.

Prof. Walter T. Rolfe, Coordinator of The Veterans Advisory Service, were present and
spoke at length on the need for more ade- quate housing facilities at the University to
take care of the returning ex-service men and their families and of graduate students who
will want to take advantage of the educational opportunities for veterans at the
